newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen stable, tone weak on results.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen stable, tone weak on results.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen stable on Tuesday as sentiment remained cautious after one of the market's largest capitalised firms Semen Gresik announced a poor first half net profit, brokers said.
"Overall sentiment is likely to remain weak after the announcement of a poor first half net profit by Semen Gresik," one broker said, adding the results were worse than expected.
Semen Gresik's poor results helped dragged down the Jakarta composite index on Monday as the index fell 3.06 points, or 0.42 percent, to close at 718.71 points.
Semen Gresik said on Monday it posted a net profit of 87.37 billion rupiah in the first six months of 1997 against 115.65 billion rupiah in the same period of last year.
Large mining firms Tambang Timah and Inco had also earlier announced poor first half results.

Brokers said stocks to watch included the pharmaceutical firm Kalbe Farma after a Media Indonesia reported that around 70 employees of the company had lodged complains with the National Human Rights Commission over their allegedly unfair dismissals.
